Q106C.0: Interviewer reports no approach by community or party representatives; this is an observed absence of contact, not evidence of respondent non-partisanship.
Q106C.1: Interviewer reports having been approached by community and/or political party representatives, an actor-side event rather than a respondent attitude.

Q106D.0: Interviewer records no felt threat across the interview; this distinguishes felt safety from absence of any physical threat item.
Q106D.1: Interviewer records having felt threatened, a subjective apprehension that does not by itself establish any physical act.

Q106E.0: Interviewer reports no physical threat occurred; distinct from felt threat because bodily threat is not required for Q106D Yes.
Q106E.1: Interviewer reports an actual physical threat, separating bodily threat from the broader felt-threat item.

Q109F.1: Interviewer judges the respondent candid; an attributed demeanor, not a verified truthfulness test.
Q109F.2: Interviewer places candor between honest and misleading, a middle position on one interviewer-assessed predicate.
Q109F.3: Interviewer judges the respondent misleading, an evaluative attribution by the fieldworker rather than a recorded false statement.

Q28.1: Strongest endorsement of the view that an elected president need not be bound by laws or courts he deems wrong.
Q28.2: Milder endorsement of presidential non-binding to law and courts; same statement, weaker intensity.
Q28.3: Milder endorsement of obligatory presidential obedience to law and courts; same statement, weaker intensity than code 4.
Q28.4: Strongest endorsement of the view that the president must always obey laws and courts.
Q28.5: Rejects both statements; this is a distinct neither-position, not a missing or refused response.
Q28.-1: Source-native missing marker; not an answer about presidential obedience.
Q28.8: Explicit refusal to choose; distinct from a substantive neither and from not-asked.
Q28.9: Don't know; an admission of no position, distinct from refusal and from the neither option.
Q28.94: Country-level non-administration marker; this field was not asked in that country, not a respondent answer.

Q19A.1: Strongest endorsement of the government-as-boss statement.
Q19A.2: Milder endorsement of the government-as-boss statement.
Q19A.3: Milder endorsement of the government-as-employee statement.
Q19A.4: Strongest endorsement of the government-as-employee statement.
Q19A.5: Rejects both analogies; a distinct neither position, not a missing answer.
Q19A.-1: Source-native missing marker, not a stance on the boss/employee analogy.
Q19A.8: Explicit refusal, distinct from neither and from don't know.
Q19A.9: Don't know, an absence of stance distinct from refusal.

Q19B.1: Strongest endorsement of the view that elected officials should do what voters demand.
Q19B.2: Milder endorsement of the voters-demand statement.
Q19B.3: Milder endorsement of the leaders-follow-own-ideas statement.
Q19B.4: Strongest endorsement of the leaders-follow-own-ideas statement.
Q19B.5: Rejects both statements; a substantive neither, not a missing value.
Q19B.94: Field not asked in the country; a design exclusion, not a respondent answer.
Q19B.997: Not applicable marker, a route exclusion distinct from missing.

Q21A.1: Strongest rejection of the claim that men should have more job rights when jobs are scarce.
Q21A.2: Milder rejection of the men-first job-rights claim.
Q21A.3: Neither agreement nor disagreement with the men-first job-rights claim; a distinct neutral stance.
Q21A.4: Endorsement that men should have more job rights when jobs are scarce.
Q21A.5: Strongest endorsement of the men-first job-rights claim.
Q21A.-1: Source-native missing marker, not a stance.

Q22B.3: Neither approval nor disapproval of army rule; distinct from refusal.

Q39B.0: Respondent believes ordinary people can report corruption without fear.
Q39B.1: Respondent believes reporting carries retaliation risk; the contrast is a risk belief, not a reported incident.
Q39B.-1: Source-native missing marker, not a risk judgment.

Q49A.1: Strongest denial that women and men have equal wage-job opportunities today.
Q49A.2: Milder denial of equal wage-job opportunities.
Q49A.3: Neither agreement nor disagreement about equal wage-job opportunities.
Q49A.4: Agreement that women and men have equal wage-job opportunities today.
Q49A.5: Strongest affirmation of equal wage-job opportunities.

Q53C.1: Judges community criticism, harassment, or shaming of a woman reporting GBV as very unlikely.
Q53C.2: Judges such community reaction as somewhat unlikely.
Q53C.3: Judges such community reaction as somewhat likely.
Q53C.4: Judges community shaming of a woman reporting GBV as very likely.
Q53C.-1: Source-native missing marker, not a likelihood judgment.
Q53C.6: Refusal code present as an alternative spelling of refusal alongside code 8.
Q53C.8: Refusal code; duplicated refusal label in the same value set.

Q64A.1: Belief that government will be very unprepared for future health emergencies.
Q64A.2: Belief that government will be somewhat unprepared.
Q64A.3: Belief that government will be somewhat prepared.
Q64A.4: Belief that government will be very prepared.

Q90F.0: Respondent and household lack any mobile phone; no ownership.
Q90F.1: Ownership exists only at household level, not personal possession.
Q90F.2: Respondent personally owns a mobile phone.

Q90G.0: Phone exists but lacks internet access.
Q90G.1: Phone has internet access; personal-use capability rather than ownership.
Q90G.7: Not applicable marker, presumably for respondents lacking a phone; a route exclusion not equivalent to missing.

evidence.quote: Were you approached by community and/or political party representatives?

claims.text: Two-valued interviewer-reported event: whether community or party representatives made an approach, an external actor's initiative rather than respondent partisanship; collapsed 0/1 would remove the distinction between no contact and actual approach.

evidence.quote: Did you feel threatened during the interview?

claims.text: Binary interviewer-side felt-threat report about this interview; the 'No' is an absence of felt threat, not evidence that no coercion existed.

evidence.quote: Were you physically threatened during the interview?

claims.text: Binary report of bodily threat during the interview; unlike Q106D it requires a physical act, so a felt threat need not imply this code.

Three-position interviewer judgment of respondent candor on one predicate; 'In between' is a genuine middle value, not missingness, and the scale is attributed demeanor rather than measured truthfulness.

evidence.quote: The [president] must always obey the laws and the courts

claims.text: Five substantive positions on one forced choice between presidential non-binding to law/courts and obligatory obedience, with intensity ordered toward each statement plus a neither option; 94 marks country non-administration.

evidence.quote: The government is like the people's boss

claims.text: Forced choice between boss-like and employee-like government; the neither code preserves rejection of both analogies as distinct from refused and don't know.

evidence.quote: Our elected officials should listen to voters' views and do what they demand

claims.text: Same five-position agree-with-statement scale as Q19A but a different predicate (delegation versus responsiveness), and it uniquely carries 94 not-asked plus 997 not-applicable state codes.

evidence.quote: when jobs are scarce, men should have more rights to a job than women

claims.text: Five-point disagreement-to-agreement scale on a scarcity-conditional gender job-rights claim; code 1 is strongest disagreement, so low codes do not mean support for the statement.

evidence.quote: the army comes in to govern the country?

claims.text: Five-point disapproval-to-approval scale on a specific hypothetical alternative, army government; an endorsement judgment, not a report that a coup occurred.

evidence.quote: can ordinary people report incidents of corruption without fear

claims.text: Nominal two-way belief contrast coded 0/1 where 0 is the favorable 'without fear' state; ordinally-shaped codes here do not imply an increasing scale.

evidence.quote: in our country today, women and men have equal opportunities to get a job that pays a wage or salary

claims.text: Five-point agree/disagree scale on a present-tense opportunity statement limited to paid wage employment; agreement is a belief about opportunity, not an observed wage gap.

evidence.quote: she will be criticized, harassed, or shamed by others in the community

claims.text: Four-point unlikely-to-likely judgment about a hypothetical community reaction; the value set anomalously carries two refusal labels (6 and 8), so refusal is not single-valued here.

evidence.quote: how prepared or unprepared do you think the government will be

claims.text: Four-point very unprepared to very prepared forward-looking expectation about future emergency readiness; a prediction, not an assessment of past COVID response.

evidence.quote: Does anyone else in your household own one: mobile phone?

claims.text: Three substantive states distinguishing no household phone from household-only ownership from personal ownership; collapsing 1 and 2 would erase the personal-versus-shared access distinction.

evidence.quote: Does your phone have access to the internet?

claims.text: Binary internet-access capability of the respondent's phone, with a separate not-applicable state; this measures connectivity of a possessed device, not frequency of internet use.

holds.missing: No interviewer identifier in the supplied selected fields linking reports to who conducted each interview.
holds.why: Interviewer-attributed demeanour and threat reports cannot be clustered or tested for interviewer effects within this packet.

holds.missing: No documentation distinguishing the two refusal codes 6 and 8 in this field.
holds.why: Cannot determine whether refusal here is one act with duplicate labels or two distinct nonresponse circumstances.

holds.missing: Country frame absent from the supplied selected fields; several carry country-specific exclusion codes.
holds.why: Cannot fix which country or wave the not-asked exclusion applies to, so route exclusions cannot be interpreted.
